episodes.about: The most consequential AI announcements this week may be the ones getting the least attention: Microsoft's MAI Base 2 and Meta's Muse Spark Open, and what they mean for how businesses use, customize, and pay for AI. Headlines include Anthropic's embedded safety evaluators, Cognition's performance-based token budgets, and a community-built AI battle royale.
episodes.title: The Most Important AI News This Week Is Getting Overlooked
episodes.why: Microsoft's MAI Base 2 and Meta's Muse Spark Open landed with little fanfare - NLW argues they change how companies buy and customize AI more than the week's bigger headlines.

episodes.about: OpenAI president Greg Brockman joins Sarah Guo and Elad Gil on what the latest frontier models change for science and security: AI agents solving nearly 400 century-old math problems, drug discovery past the biology data bottleneck, a critical window to use AI to find and fix vulnerabilities before attackers do, and proactive always-on agents like Dots.
episodes.title: The Changing Physics of Cybersecurity and Drug Development with OpenAI President Greg Brockman
episodes.why: Brockman puts numbers on it: nearly 400 century-old math problems solved by agents, and a closing window to use the same capability to patch vulnerabilities first.

episodes.about: Zocdoc CEO Oliver Kharraz argues the hard part of booking care is not finding a doctor but accurate availability, and explains why Zocdoc is opening the scheduling infrastructure it built over nearly 20 years to AI agents, insurers, and other platforms - including a partnership with Gemini - so appointments can be booked wherever a patient starts.
episodes.title: Why AI Could Finally Fix Healthcare Access | Zocdoc CEO Oliver Kharraz
episodes.why: Out this morning: Zocdoc is opening its booking rails to AI agents and Gemini, so scheduling a doctor may soon happen inside the chat instead of on a website.

episodes.about: Top AI leaders are saying their own technology is moving too fast and asking to be regulated, but none of them slows down for fear of being left behind. Planet Money looks to 1975, when gene-splicing scientists gathered at Asilomar and collectively hit pause on their own field, for a way out of the collective action problem.
episodes.title: Wanna slow down AI? These biologists can help.
episodes.why: Discovery pick - NPR's economics show, in plain language: in 1975 biologists paused gene-splicing on purpose at Asilomar. AI's leaders say they want the same brake and cannot find it.

episodes.about: A frontier model spent weeks troubleshooting a Mac Mail slowdown and kept digging down the same wrong path; the answer was there once the question changed. The hosts break down why agents get locked into a path they have already taken and the practical fixes - reframing the question, spinning up a fresh agent for a second opinion - plus what changes when GrokBot and MCP connections give AI access to your own data.
episodes.title: AI Tunnel Vision and Data Access
episodes.why: Discovery pick - a long-running entrepreneurs' show: a frontier model wasted weeks on a Mac Mail problem by refusing to reframe it, and the fixes are ones you can use today.
